approachQuestion.prompt:
Ranked channel reading

A read-only r by c matrix has each row sorted nondecreasingly, with no column ordering promised. Return the kth smallest cell value across all rows, counting duplicates separately. 1<=r,c<=1000; values are integers in [0,U], 1<=U<=10^9; 1<=k<=r*c. Examples: [[1,8],[2,4]], k=3 -> 4; [[2,2],[2,9]], k=2 -> 2. Use a value-domain search with row-independent counts; within that strategy minimize worst-case work and memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Binary-search candidate values v in [0,U]. For each v, upper-bound search each row to count values <=v; add those counts and retain the first v whose total is >=k.
options.feedback: Cumulative rank is monotone in candidate value even though equality frequencies are not; sorted rows make each cumulative count searchable.

options.text: Use the same value search but copy each row before performing its upper-bound count.
options.feedback: The count and result are correct, but copying rows adds avoidable work and storage.

options.text: Count only entries equal to v and treat a count >=k as the search feasibility predicate.
options.feedback: For [[1,8],[2,4]], k=3 no value occurs three times, although the third smallest value exists and is 4. Equality counts are not cumulative ranks or monotone.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Analyze only iterative value search with full row-independent upper-bound counts per candidate. U is the supplied bound; no heaps, copies, recursion or hashing. Random access and fixed-width operations are constant time. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(r log(c + 1) log(U + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(r log(c + 1) log(U + 2)) time, O(r*c + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Multiply value-range search iterations by the cost of all row-bound searches.
details: For each of O(log(U+2)) candidate values, r rows each require O(log(c+1)) upper-bound comparisons. These nested costs multiply. The iterative searches reuse scalar bounds and accumulate one count without storing a rank table.
“O(r log(c + 1) log(U + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Cumulative rank is monotone in candidate value even though equality frequencies are not; sorted rows make each cumulative count searchable.
“O(r log(c + 1) log(U + 2)) time, O(r*c + 1) auxiliary space”: Each row search uses scalar bounds and reads the original matrix directly; expanded value/cell arrays are never materialized.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each candidate value requires r row counts and the candidate range itself needs repeated halvings.
